capabilities: Catalog books as one Markdown note each, with metadata in frontmatter
Rate books via weighted yes/no question sets that produce a 0-10 ARL score and stars
Browse a sortable, searchable library list and a draggable virtual bookshelf with saved arrangements
Log reading sessions with progress bars, pages-per-day charts, characters, quotes and image galleries
Set reading goals per day/week/month/year with medals, streaks and yearly summaries
extras: Requires Obsidian 1.13.0 or later; English and Italian interface switchable live; works on desktop and mobile; the manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
motivation: The author built the virtual library to recreate the spatial memory of a real bookshelf, where a book is a physical object with a place, not a row in a table.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to catalog a book collection, rate books with a structured and comparable method, or track reading sessions, goals and yearly statistics.

relations.evidence: you can query it with Dataview, Bases, or any tool

summary: Personal library manager that catalogs books as Markdown notes, rates them with weighted yes/no question sets (ARL score 0-10), and tracks reading progress and goals.
